name: Turn a research question into hypotheses
description: Analyse a research question, develop testable hypotheses, review them critically and derive an experimental plan.
input:
SYNTHETIC SAMPLE DATA – entirely fictional, for trying things out only.

Research question: Can the curing temperature of our powder coating PL-7 be reduced from 180 °C to 165 °C
without harming adhesion on galvanised steel? The aim is to save around 10 % energy in the oven.

Pilot test (5 panels each, cross-cut rating according to ISO 2409, 0 = best adhesion, 5 = worst):
- 180 °C, 15 min: 0, 0, 1, 0, 1
- 165 °C, 15 min: 1, 0, 2, 1, 1
- 165 °C, 20 min: 0, 1, 0, 1, 0

Constraints: 40 test panels available per week, oven free for trials two days a week,
pre-treatment of the panels has so far been done on two different days.

guide.problem: Good research starts with a precise, testable question. The workflow breaks down a research question, formulates hypotheses, has them criticised methodologically and derives a realistic experimental plan.
guide.flow: A sequential chain with a look back: the analyst clarifies variables and assumptions, the hypothesis agent formulates testable hypotheses with null hypotheses, the methods critic checks them against the pilot data with the calculator tool and names confounders. The experiment planner uses hypotheses and critique together.
guide.input: A research question with its aim, existing data from pilot tests and constraints such as material, time and equipment. You can attach measurement data and documents as files; the sample file contains the pilot test ratings per panel.
guide.result: An experiment plan with hypotheses, factors and levels, sample size, measurement method, analysis and stopping criteria, plus the open risks, also as a Word file. The experiment planner proposes the plan for knowledge; you decide whether it is stored.
guide.adapt: Replace the question and pilot test with your own and attach measurement data directly. Literature you need again and again can be uploaded as knowledge in “Search” mode and assigned to the question analyst so that it works with quotations. Add your statistical guidelines to the methods critic.

framing.name: Question analyst
framing.description: Clarifies aim, variables, constraints and knowledge gaps.
framing.system: You are a research associate who structures research questions. Break the question down into aim, independent and dependent variables, possible confounders and constraints. Summarise what the existing data shows and what it does not, and separate established knowledge from conjecture.

hypotheses.name: Hypothesis developer
hypotheses.description: Formulates testable hypotheses with predictions and null hypotheses.
hypotheses.system: You formulate scientific hypotheses. Derive three to five testable hypotheses from the analysis. For each, state the null hypothesis, a measurable prediction, the measurement method and what counts as confirmation or refutation. Order them by relevance to the aim.
hypotheses.task:
Develop hypotheses based on this analysis:

{{node:framing}}

critic.name: Methods critic
critic.description: Checks hypotheses for testability, confounders and the data available.
critic.system: You are a strict methodologist and reviewer. Check each hypothesis for falsifiability, measurability, confounders and bias. Evaluate the available pilot data with the calculator tool (for example means and ranges) and judge whether the data allows a statement. State which hypotheses should be rejected, sharpened or kept.

design.name: Experiment planner
design.description: Derives an experimental plan from the hypotheses and the critique.
design.system: You plan experiments following the principles of design of experiments. For the hypotheses that were kept, design an experimental plan: factors and levels, replications, randomisation and blocking against confounders, measurement method, analysis method, stopping and success criteria, and a schedule that fits the constraints. Finish with the open risks.

research_files.label: Research documents
research_files.description: Optional: measurement data (CSV, Excel, JSON) and documents such as test reports or papers (PDF, Word, Markdown), up to 6 files. Without files, the details in the text apply.
